label: <DEL> step, strongest when the first token is h/z/b/f
explanation: Almost a pure delimiter-step unit: 97% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> input (recall_idx 0). It never fires in the copy phase and only weakly fires late in the original phase (about 3% of mass). It fires on just 12% of <DEL> steps, and which ones depends mostly on the first original token: h, z, b, f (lift 3.3-4.9x) give about 62% of the mass. Digits and p/l as first token come next. A second token z also helps (the top examples are f z ..., h z ..., z z ...). Rate falls slowly as L grows. The predicate phase==1 & first token in {h,z,b,f} reaches only F1 about 0.49 on dev; adding orig(1)==z or more first-token values trades precision for recall without raising F1. Plain phase==1 has 95% recall but 12% precision. Magnitude grows with the first-token effect: the predicate covers 72% of top-quartile activations but only 34% of bottom-quartile ones.
